questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The location across the globe, the different climate and wildlife, and the different influences from nearby countries.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This mark is shaped by my partner traveling with me (very positive).

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
There were information-filled emails before we arrived and an online meeting where we could ask for clarification. However, it was still a bit confusing to understand how things worked when we hadn't visited the university in person yet and because of the sheer size of Monash. 
During Orientation Week on campus, there was a lot of signage on where to go and another meeting on where to ask for help, etc. In this sense, it was easy once we arrived.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not require assistance after the information meeting.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very clear.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Since I was travelling with my partner and we split the bills, we went directly on Airbnb and found a budget-friendly place easily. I think we were very lucky, because many of the Danes I met struggled with finding affordable accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Make sure that everything (water, electricity, internet) is included or at least that it is transparent what it costs.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Mainly for BA students. The MA students I met who lived on campus voiced the same concern.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The Monash Handbook 2025 was very hard to find. Perhaps because of the sheer size of the institution. Confusion (maybe discrepancy but maybe just confusion) between the Handbook and Allocate.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
First: read the handbook and choose courses (make sure they correspond to UCPH's course criteria)
Later: choose times on Allocate

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email to the program officers (very quick response time).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fortunately, I got every class I wanted at the times I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit daunting and confusing, but the program officers are very quick to respond to questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was enrolled in courses in communications and, as advertised, they were very hands-on. For example, I had a course where we ran weekly focus groups and a photography course where we got plenty of time to practice and receive feedback on our work. I had one course where we had weekly blogs, but this format did not work because they only gave us feedback on our weekly work a month after the entire course had finished. This was an exception as the other courses were good at giving feedback.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: This was the last semester of my Master's degree and the first MA semester for many of the people in my classes. There is a participation-expectation in class discussions during the tutorials. I found this easy enough because I kept up with the readings. This is similar to UCPH, however, many of my international student friends expressed that it was hard to do in-class discussions because it was not expected of them during their BA.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is more handheld in the sense that rubrics are given for assignments that you have to follow (cookie-cutter in this way). I liked that there were many different assignments with different grade weights compared to the final paper and final grade system at UCPH (humanities). Because of how big the university is, we had an online lecture and then there were many (so many!) workshops with a tutor and us students (20 or so). This was much different than my small UCPH classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Photography 
Understanding Media Audiences 
Principles of Global Media and Communication
Cultural Policy

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Since we ran focus groups every week in Understanding Media Audiences, this was a great chance to properly get to know fellow students. The same goes for photography where we took portraits in groups. I formed great friendships in these classes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing comes to mind. All the utilities were included where we were staying.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Beer was pricey. Eating out was cheaper than in Denmark, as expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They felt mostly directed to BA students and Australian BA students are generally younger than Danish university students. On the other hand, some of my MA friends were part of some clubs, however, they were international students and not exchange students, meaning that they were at Monash for their entire degree and not just one semester.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The clubs my friends (see above) were part of were career-oriented communications clubs. There were also some creative ones, but I do not remember those well. I was not interested in joining clubs while on my MA exchange because I had the impression that they were mainly directed to MA students. While on my BA exchange in another Anglophone country, I did participate in many clubs and found it very fun and a good way to meet people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think that there were some hiking ones, which would be fun, especially if you are coming here on your own.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I loved all the museums from galleries in CBD to more niche ones like the Tram Museum in Hawthorn. I would recommend spending time in different neighbourhoods for their distinct atmospheres (Brunswick, the Docks, Prahran etc.). I would also recommend going outside of the city (public transportation) for hikes (e.g. Dandenong).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Being part Anglo myself, there was nothing entirely shocking about the local culture. It was what I expected.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My biggest tip is to get people's socials and not be shy to write to them and ask to grab a coffee or something.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: My tutorials consisted 98% of Chinese international students, so that was a much different culture than I was expecting (more Australian) when I entered the classrooms. During class, they seemed a little intimidated by the setting and language, and often spoke Chinese amongst themselves. It was a little challenging to get to know them at first but as soon as I saw them outside of class they were super warm and friendly, somehow remembered my name, and made me feel included in their conversations. What I want to illustrate is that settings, such as classroom culture, may change people, and that it can be challenging at times to understand someone from one particular setting.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated my friendships with the Chinese international students because they were all so kind and we genuinely wanted to understand each other. I also really appreciated how gregarious Australians are (generalization, but I found that being talkative is a large part of the culture).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. It is over before you know it so enjoy it while it lasts. 
2. Keeping up with the readings makes it easier in the long run. 
3. Explore the city and surrounding areas as much as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I have said what I wanted to say.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My friendships with people from different cultures than mine.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Honestly, the time and effort it takes to fly halfway across the globe.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
